internal.title: Incident Report: Elevated Error Rate in flagd Service - Escalated
internal.body:
At 12:01 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for a high error rate in the flagd service. Initial diagnosis focused on the frontend component with a proposed restart action. However, the restart action was blocked due to missing dry-run permissions in this deployment environment. Subsequent replans also identified that restart_service was unavailable for the frontend-proxy, leading to no actionable remediation steps within the automated system.

Due to lack of evidence and inability to perform automated recovery, the incident was escalated to the on-call engineer at 12:21 UTC for manual investigation and resolution.

No recovery was verified during the automated diagnosis phase, so root cause remains undetermined at this stage.

Timeline highlights:
- 12:01:14 UTC: Alert received for high error rate
- 12:20:54 UTC: Diagnosis round 1 proposed frontend restart
- 12:20:58 UTC: Proposal refused due to dry_run_missing
- 12:21:00 to 12:21:07 UTC: Replans identified restart_service unavailable
- 12:21:11 UTC: Incident escalated to on-call engineer

Next steps include manual investigation and further diagnostics by the engineering team.

external.title: Service Interruption Notice: Elevated Error Rates Detected
external.body:
On 2026-11-08 starting at approximately 12:01 UTC, our monitoring systems detected elevated error rates affecting the flagd service. This may have impacted service reliability for some customers. Our automated systems attempted recovery actions but were unable to resolve the issue automatically. The incident has been escalated to our engineering team for further investigation and resolution.

We apologize for any inconvenience caused and appreciate your patience as we work to restore full service.

action_items: Review and enable dry-run permissions for restart_service actions in all deployment environments.
Enhance guardrail messaging to include fallback recovery options or manual intervention steps when automated actions are blocked.
Conduct a post-incident review with the engineering team to identify root cause and implement permanent fixes.
